According to Liverpool's seasoned full-back Andy Robertson, the primary factor that will determine the success of Arne Slot’s inaugural season as manager will be the squad's ability to significantly bolster its defensive performance. Robertson identifies a fortified defense as the fundamental ingredient for mounting a credible challenge for the league title. While the team has begun the new campaign on an encouraging note, securing clean sheets in their first two fixtures, a formidable challenge awaits them on the horizon. Their upcoming journey to Old Trafford to face rivals Manchester United is poised to be a much more rigorous examination of their defensive capabilities. The initial matches against Ipswich and Brentford, while resulting in a perfect start for the new manager by preventing any goals, are not seen as the ultimate test. This new emphasis on defensive solidity comes in the wake of a previous season where Liverpool, despite finishing a respectable third, displayed a notable vulnerability at the back. The club conceded a total of 41 goals across the 38-game league season, a figure that was substantially higher than their main competitors. This tally was seven goals more than the champions, Manchester City, and a significant twelve more than the runners-up, Arsenal, highlighting a clear area for necessary improvement if they hope to climb higher in the standings.

handle the offensive threats of top-tier opposition. Robertson explicitly pointed to the statistical discrepancy from the previous campaign as a critical lesson. He articulated that even during the periods when Liverpool were firmly in contention for the title, a deeper look at the analytics revealed they were consistently allowing more goal-scoring opportunities to their opponents than either Arsenal or Manchester City were. This underlying fragility, a tendency to be more open and concede more chances, was a high-risk strategy that ultimately proved to be their undoing. In Robertson’s view, when a team continuously plays in a manner that invites pressure and gives opponents opportunities, it is only a matter of time before they are severely penalized for it in a crucial match. That inevitable punishment, he suggests, is precisely what derailed their title aspirations last season. In contrast, the start to the current season has been a source of considerable optimism. "I think in the first two games, you’ve seen that, two clean sheets, which we couldn’t have asked for better,” Robertson stated, expressing his satisfaction with the initial defensive displays. This perfect defensive record provides a strong foundation upon which the team can build confidence under Slot’s new leadership.

The Scottish captain's hope is that this newfound defensive resilience is not a fleeting trend but the beginning of a sustained strategic shift for the team. He voiced a clear objective to maintain this level of performance, starting with the immediate challenge of containing Manchester United's attack. “We hope that we can keep that going and we hope that we can limit Man United to the chances,” he remarked, underscoring the importance of the upcoming derby. Looking beyond that single fixture, the ambition is to apply this principle consistently throughout the season against every opponent they face following the international break. Robertson’s reflection on the previous year indicates a mature understanding within the squad that a leaky defense is not a sustainable model for championship success. The acknowledgment that they were conceding too many chances, even when winning, points to a collective realization that a more controlled and disciplined approach is required. His comments signal a clear intent from the players to embrace a philosophy centered on minimizing opponent opportunities, recognizing that this defensive platform is what will ultimately enable their potent attack to secure the points needed for a genuine title fight.
